attributes.description: Date of the buyer's most recent formal performance review. Used to track review cycles and identify buyers due for evaluation.

attributes.name: markdown_percentage_limit
attributes.description: Maximum allowable markdown percentage the buyer can authorize without additional approval. Expressed as a percentage of original retail price (e.g., 30.00 means up to 30% markdown is allowed).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Policy

attributes.name: office_location_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the physical office or buying center where the buyer is based. Used for travel expense allocation and regional vendor assignments.

attributes.name: otb_budget_limit
attributes.description: Total OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocated to this buyer for the current fiscal period. Represents the maximum inventory investment the buyer can commit to across all assigned categories.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - OTB Planning

attributes.name: phone_number
attributes.description: Primary business phone number for the buyer. Used for vendor negotiations and internal escalations.

attributes.name: preferred_vendor_count
attributes.description: Number of preferred or strategic vendors the buyer actively manages relationships with. Used to assess vendor portfolio concentration and diversification strategy.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Vendor Management

attributes.name: private_label_focus_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the buyer has primary responsibility for private label (store brand) product development and sourcing. True if the buyer manages private label assortments.

attributes.name: sell_through_rate_target
attributes.description: Target sell-through rate percentage assigned to the buyer for their assigned categories. Represents the percentage of inventory that should be sold within a defined period (typically a season). Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 85.00 means 85% of inventory should sell through).

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date the buyer left the organization or was terminated. Null for active employees. Triggers reassignment of assigned categories and vendors.

attributes.name: vendor_negotiation_rating
attributes.description: Performance rating reflecting the buyer's effectiveness in negotiating favorable commercial terms with vendors. Based on achieved cost reductions, payment terms, and markdown allowances.

attributes.name: years_of_buying_experience
attributes.description: Total number of years the individual has worked in merchandise buying roles, including experience prior to joining the current organization. Used for capability assessment and succession planning.

products.name: season
products.description: Reference master for retail planning seasons and fiscal periods used to scope merchandise plans, OTB budgets, assortment plans, and buying commitments. Captures season code (e.g., SS24, FW24), season name, fiscal year, start and end dates, key milestone dates (line review, buy deadline, first receipt, markdown entry, clearance exit), and season status (planning, open-to-buy, in-season, post-season). Provides the temporal backbone for all merchandising planning and performance measurement.

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the retail planning season. Primary key.

attributes.name: semantic_layer_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.semantic_layer_entity. Business justification: Season is a fundamental time-based dimension in retail analytics. Sales planning, inventory forecasting, and assortment analysis all use season as a key dimension. Semantic layer defines season entity

attributes.name: assortment_breadth_target
attributes.description: The target number of distinct product categories to be carried during this season. Represents the range of categories. Drives overall merchandising strategy and store space allocation.

attributes.name: assortment_depth_target
attributes.description: The target number of SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) within each product category for this season. Represents the variety within categories. Drives category management and buying decisions.

attributes.name: buy_deadline_date
attributes.description: The final date by which all purchase orders for the season must be committed to vendors. Ensures timely receipt of merchandise for season launch.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: clearance_exit_date
attributes.description: The target date by which all seasonal merchandise should be sold through or removed from active selling floor. Marks the end of clearance activities.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Calendar

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the season record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the OTB budget and financial planning (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across regions.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date when the season officially ends. Marks the transition to post-season analysis and clearance activities.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: first_receipt_date
attributes.description: The target date for the first merchandise receipts to arrive at distribution centers or stores for the season. Marks the beginning of inventory flow.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this season belongs (e.g., 2024). Aligns season planning with financial reporting periods.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the season is currently active for planning or operational use. True if the season is in planning, open-to-buy, or in-season status. False if post-season or closed.

attributes.name: line_review_date
attributes.description: Key milestone date when the merchandising team reviews and approves the product line assortment for the season. Critical gate for buying decisions.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: markdown_entry_date
attributes.description: The date when initial markdown pricing strategies are activated to accelerate sell-through of seasonal merchandise. Signals transition to promotional phase.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Calendar

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, strategic notes, or special considerations for the season (e.g., market trends, competitive landscape, promotional themes). Used by merchandising planners.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: otb_budget_amount
attributes.description: The total Open to Buy budget allocated for this season in the base currency. Represents the planned purchase commitment for merchandise. Critical for financial planning and vendor negotiations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - OTB Planning

attributes.name: planning_start_date
attributes.description: The date when pre-season planning activities begin, including assortment planning, OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocation, and category strategy development.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Planning

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code representing the season (e.g., SS24 for Spring/Summer 2024, FW24 for Fall/Winter 2024). Used as the business identifier across merchandising systems.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the season (e.g., Spring/Summer 2024, Holiday 2024, Back-to-School 2024). Human-readable label for business users.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the season. Planning: pre-season planning phase. Open-to-Buy: OTB budgets active, buying in progress. In-Season: merchandise on floor, active selling. Post-Season: season ended, analysis and clearance. Closed: season archived.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_type
attributes.description: Classification of the season by merchandising cycle (e.g., spring/summer, fall/winter, holiday, back-to-school). Drives assortment planning and buying strategies.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when the season officially begins for merchandising and planning purposes. Marks the start of in-season operations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: target_gmroi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Target Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
attributes.description: The target GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) ratio for the season. Measures the profitability of inventory investment. Key performance metric for merchandising effectiveness.

attributes.name: target_inventory_turns
attributes.description: The target number of times inventory should turn over during the season. Higher turns indicate more efficient inventory management. Key metric for supply chain and merchandising performance.

attributes.name: target_sell_through_rate
attributes.description: The target percentage of seasonal inventory that should be sold at full price before markdowns begin. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 75.00 for 75%). Drives inventory planning and markdown timing.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the season record was last modified. Audit trail for change tracking and data governance.

products.name: otb_budget
products.description: Open to Buy (OTB) budget record representing the financial control mechanism that governs merchandise buying spend. Tracks planned receipts at cost, actual receipts, committed orders (on-order), available OTB balance, and budget adjustments (transfers, increases, decreases) by department, category, buyer, and season. Updated in near-real-time as buying orders are placed. The authoritative record for whether a buyer has remaining budget authority to commit new purchases. Sourced from ORMS and reconciled with SAP S/4HANA MM.

attributes.name: otb_budget_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the Open to Buy budget record. Primary key for the OTB budget entity.

attributes.name: assortment_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise assortment plan that this OTB budget supports. Links budget allocation to the strategic assortment depth and breadth decisions.

attributes.name: budget_owner_associate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: OTB budgets require a designated budget owner/planner for accountability, approval workflows, and audit trails. Retail operations track who is responsible for managing each budget allocation. Existing

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise buyer responsible for managing this OTB budget. The buyer has authority to commit purchases within the available budget balance.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise category within the department for which this OTB budget applies. Categories provide finer product segmentation (e.g., Men's Shirts, Laptops, Bedding).

attributes.name: cluster_id
attributes.description: Reference to the store cluster or store group for which this OTB budget is allocated. Store clusters group stores with similar assortment needs, demographics, or performance characteristics.

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise department for which this OTB budget is allocated. Departments represent high-level product groupings (e.g., Apparel, Electronics, Home Goods).

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: OTB budgets map to specific GL accounts (inventory, COGS) for financial posting when purchase orders are received. Required for three-way match, GL coding, and financial statement preparation.

attributes.name: gmroi_kpi_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.kpi_definition. Business justification: OTB budget tracking measures performance against KPIs (gmroi_target, inventory_turn_target, sell_through_target_pct). Budget variance reports reference KPI definitions for standardized calculation for

attributes.name: item_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.item_hierarchy. Business justification: OTB budgets are allocated to specific merchandise hierarchy nodes. Essential for buyer authority limits, budget reconciliation, receipt planning, and financial control in retail buying operations and

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise season or planning period for which this OTB budget is allocated (e.g., Spring 2024, Holiday 2024, Back-to-School 2024).

attributes.name: actual_receipts_at_cost
attributes.description: The total actual merchandise receipts at cost that have been received into inventory during this budget period. Updated as goods receipts are posted from purchase orders.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The approval status of the OTB budget. Pending = awaiting review; Approved = authorized for buyer use; Rejected = not approved and requires revision.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the merchandising leader or financial controller who approved this OTB budget. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget was approved. Marks the point at which the budget became active and available for buyer commitments.

attributes.name: available_otb_balance
attributes.description: The remaining budget balance available for new purchase commitments. Calculated as: Planned Receipts + Adjustments - Actual Receipts - Committed Amount. This is the authoritative field that determines whether a buyer can place new orders.

attributes.name: budget_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The cumulative net adjustment to the original planned receipts budget. Includes increases, decreases, and transfers from other budgets. Positive values increase available OTB; negative values decrease it.

attributes.name: budget_decrease_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget decreases applied to this OTB budget. Decreases may occur due to lower-than-expected sales, inventory overstock, or strategic reallocation to other categories.

attributes.name: budget_end_date
attributes.description: The effective end date of the OTB budget period. After this date, the budget is typically closed and no further commitments are allowed unless extended.

attributes.name: budget_increase_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget increases applied to this OTB budget. Increases are typically approved by senior merchandising leadership to support higher-than-planned demand or strategic opportunities.

attributes.name: budget_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name for the OTB budget, typically combining department, category, season, and buyer information for easy identification.

attributes.name: budget_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the OTB budget record. Used for reporting, reconciliation, and cross-system reference.

attributes.name: budget_start_date
attributes.description: The effective start date of the OTB budget period. Buyers can begin committing purchases on or after this date.

attributes.name: budget_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the OTB budget. Draft = under planning; Active = buyers can commit purchases; Frozen = temporarily locked for review; Closed = planning period ended; Cancelled = budget withdrawn.

attributes.name: budget_transfer_in_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget transferred into this OTB budget from other budgets. Transfers allow buyers to reallocate funds between categories or departments within the same season.

attributes.name: budget_transfer_out_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget transferred out of this OTB budget to other budgets. Recorded as a positive value; reduces the available OTB balance of this budget.

attributes.name: committed_amount
attributes.description: The total amount committed on open purchase orders that have not yet been received. Also known as on-order amount. Represents future obligations against the OTB budget.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary amounts in this OTB budget are expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, CAD).

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period (month or quarter) within the fiscal year for which this OTB budget is allocated. Typically 1-12 for monthly periods or 1-4 for quarterly periods.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this OTB budget applies (e.g., 2024). Used for multi-year budget tracking and financial planning alignment.

attributes.name: gmroi_target
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
attributes.description: The target GMROI ratio for this OTB budget. GMROI measures the gross margin dollars returned for every dollar invested in inventory. Used to evaluate buying efficiency and profitability.

attributes.name: inventory_turn_target
attributes.description: The target inventory turnover rate for merchandise purchased under this OTB budget. Represents the number of times inventory is sold and replaced during the budget period.

attributes.name: last_reconciliation_date
attributes.description: The date when this OTB budget was last reconciled with SAP S/4HANA MM purchase order and goods receipt data. Used to ensure data consistency between ORMS and ERP systems.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget record was last modified. Updated in near-real-time as purchase orders are placed, goods are received, or budget adjustments are made.

attributes.name: markdown_budget_pct
attributes.description: The planned markdown percentage allocated for this OTB budget. Represents the expected price reductions as a percentage of planned receipts at retail. Used for margin planning and promotional strategy.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this OTB budget. May include rationale for adjustments, special instructions, or strategic context for the buyer.

attributes.name: planned_receipts_at_cost
attributes.description: The total planned merchandise receipts at cost for this budget period. Represents the initial budget allocation before any adjustments or commitments. Expressed in the budget currency.

attributes.name: sell_through_target_pct
attributes.description: The target sell-through rate (as a percentage) for merchandise purchased under this OTB budget. Represents the percentage of inventory expected to be sold during the budget period.

products.name: buying_order
products.description: Merchandise buying order representing a committed purchase from a supplier for specific SKUs, quantities, and delivery windows. Captures order type (initial buy, reorder, opportunistic), planned receipt date, FOB terms, cost per unit, total order value, and approval status. Distinct from operational purchase orders — this is the buying decision record in ORMS.

attributes.name: buying_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the merchandise buying order record in ORMS (Oracle Retail Merchandising System). Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the merchandise buyer or purchasing agent responsible for creating and managing this buying order. Links to workforce/employee master data.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the product category within the department. Enables category-level assortment analysis and GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) tracking.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Purchase orders for fixtures, supplies, or capital items are allocated to cost centers for capex vs opex classification and budget tracking. Required for non-inventory purchase cost allocation.

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the merchandise department for which this buying order is placed. Used for category management and assortment planning.

attributes.name: destination_location_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific distribution center, store, or cross-dock facility where the merchandise will be received. Links to inventory node or store master data.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Purchase orders post to specific GL accounts (inventory, prepaid, expense) when goods are received. Essential for three-way match, accrual accounting, and financial statement accuracy.

attributes.name: import_license_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.license_permit. Business justification: Import buying orders for regulated categories (alcohol, tobacco, pharmaceuticals, firearms) require valid import licenses. Customs brokers verify license validity before shipment. Real business proces

attributes.name: otb_budget_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocation against which this buying order is committed. Used to track spending against merchandise financial plans and prevent over-buying.

attributes.name: primary_buying_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user (merchandise manager or authorized approver) who provided final approval for the buying order. Links to workforce/employee master data.

attributes.name: receiving_fulfillment_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fulfillment.node. Business justification: Inbound purchase orders must specify receiving DC/warehouse for inventory routing and capacity planning. Retail operations require knowing which fulfillment node will process incoming vendor shipments

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Buying orders are executed within specific retail seasons for merchandise planning and OTB budget tracking. Currently has season_code (STRING) which should be normalized to season_id FK. This links bu

attributes.name: supply_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.purchase_order. Business justification: Retail buying orders (merchandising procurement intent) are executed as supply chain purchase orders. Buyers track PO execution status, receipt variance, and landed cost reconciliation. This link enab

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the supplier from whom the merchandise is being purchased. Links to the supplier master data in MDM (Master Data Management).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order received final approval from authorized buyer or merchandise manager. Nullable for orders still in draft or pending approval status.

attributes.name: approval_workflow_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the approval workflow instance used to authorize this buying order. Tracks multi-level approvals based on order value thresholds and buyer authority limits.

attributes.name: cancel_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order was cancelled. Nullable for active orders. Populated when order_status transitions to cancelled.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for order cancellation. Nullable for active orders. Used for supplier performance analysis and procurement process improvement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this buying order record was first created in ORMS. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the buying order cost and pricing (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Used for multi-currency procurement and financial reporting.

attributes.name: destination_type
attributes.description: Type of destination location where the merchandise will be delivered: distribution center for centralized receiving, store for direct store delivery (DSD), cross_dock for immediate transfer, or vendor_direct for drop-ship to customer.

attributes.name: duty_cost
attributes.description: Estimated or actual customs duty and import taxes for international shipments. Used to calculate landed cost and COGS (Cost of Goods Sold).

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied to convert supplier currency to base reporting currency at the time of order creation. Used for financial consolidation and P&L (Profit and Loss) reporting.

attributes.name: fob_terms
attributes.description: Incoterms defining the point at which ownership and risk transfer from supplier to retailer. Determines freight responsibility and cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fob_origin|fob_destination|exw|fca|cif|dap|ddp — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: freight_cost
attributes.description: Estimated or actual freight and shipping cost for transporting the merchandise from supplier to destination. May be retailer-paid or supplier-paid depending on FOB terms.

attributes.name: landed_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of merchandise including product cost, freight, duties, and other charges to deliver goods to the distribution center. Used for margin analysis and pricing decisions.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this buying order record was last updated in ORMS. Tracks the most recent change to any field in the order.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and special instructions for the buying order. May include packaging requirements, labeling instructions, quality specifications, or other supplier communications.

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order was created and committed in ORMS. Represents the business event timestamp for the buying decision.

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the buying order. Human-readable order number used in communications with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the buying order in the procurement workflow. Tracks progression from draft through approval, submission to supplier, acknowledgment, receipt, and closure or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|submitted|acknowledged|in_transit|partially_received|received|closed|cancelled — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the buying order indicating the strategic purpose: initial buy for new assortment, reorder for replenishment, opportunistic for special deals, seasonal for seasonal merchandise, promotional for promotion-driven buys, or clearance for end-of-season purchases.

attributes.name: payment_terms
attributes.description: Negotiated payment terms with the supplier (e.g., Net 30, Net 60, 2/10 Net 30). Defines the payment due date and any early payment discounts.

attributes.name: planned_receipt_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the merchandise is expected to arrive at the distribution center or store. Used for inventory planning and assortment timing.

attributes.name: ship_window_end_date
attributes.description: Latest date the supplier must ship the merchandise to meet planned receipt date. Defines the end of the acceptable shipping window; late shipments may incur chargebacks.

attributes.name: ship_window_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest date the supplier is authorized to ship the merchandise. Defines the beginning of the acceptable shipping window for timely assortment flow.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the approved buying order was transmitted to the supplier via EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) or other communication channel.

attributes.name: total_order_cost
attributes.description: Total cost value of the buying order in the base currency, calculated as sum of (unit cost × quantity) across all line items. Represents the committed spend with the supplier, excluding freight and duties.

attributes.name: total_order_quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of units ordered across all SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) in this buying order. Aggregated from line-level quantities.

attributes.name: vendor_order_number
attributes.description: Supplier's own order reference number assigned when they acknowledge the buying order. Used for order tracking and supplier communication.

products.name: buying_order_line
products.description: Line-level detail of a merchandise buying order capturing individual SKU commitments including SKU/UPC, ordered quantity, unit cost, retail price, planned margin, delivery date, and allocation by store cluster. Enables SKU-level OTB tracking and receipt planning.

attributes.name: buying_order_line_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the buying order line item. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise buyer responsible for this purchase decision. Used for accountability tracking and buyer performance analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Workday HCM

attributes.name: buying_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent buying order header. Links this line item to the overall purchase order placed with the vendor.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise class within the department. Provides finer-grained categorization for assortment depth and breadth analysis.

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise department or category to which this SKU belongs. Used for OTB (Open to Buy) budget tracking and category management reporting.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Individual PO lines may post to different GL accounts based on product type (inventory vs supplies vs capital). Required for line-level GL coding and mixed-item purchase order accounting.

attributes.name: otb_budget_id
attributes.description: Reference to the OTB budget against which this line item is committed. Enables tracking of buying commitments against planned budgets by category, season, and time period.

attributes.name: po_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.po_line. Business justification: Line-level traceability from merchandising buy to supply chain PO line is essential for cost reconciliation, receipt matching, and variance analysis. Retail buyers need to track which supply chain PO

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Buying order line items are allocated to specific seasons for inventory planning and sell-through tracking. Currently has season_code (STRING) which should be normalized to season_id FK. Line-level se

attributes.name: subclass_category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise subclass within the class. Enables detailed category performance tracking and assortment optimization at the most granular level.

attributes.name: uom_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.uom. Business justification: Buying order lines specify unit of measure for ordered quantities. Must link to standardized UOM master for unit conversion, case pack calculations, receiving validation, and inventory reconciliation

attributes.name: vendor_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplier.vendor_item. Business justification: Buying order lines reference vendor-specific item numbers for procurement. Receiving systems match inbound ASNs and shipments using vendor_item mappings. Purchase orders transmitted via EDI include ve

attributes.name: allocation_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of this SKU allocated to the specified store cluster. Supports pre-distribution planning and ensures inventory is directed to the right locations based on demand forecasts.

attributes.name: cancel_date
attributes.description: Date after which the retailer reserves the right to cancel this line item if not received. Enforces vendor compliance with delivery commitments and protects against late shipments.

attributes.name: cancelled_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity cancelled by either the retailer or vendor for this line item. Tracks order changes and impacts OTB budget availability and assortment plans.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this buying order line record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and order lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the cost and retail price amounts. Supports multi-currency procurement for international vendor sourcing.

attributes.name: delivery_date
attributes.description: Expected delivery date for this line item to the distribution center or store. Used for receipt planning, inventory replenishment scheduling, and vendor performance tracking.

attributes.name: drop_ship_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this line item will be drop shipped directly from vendor to customer rather than through the retailers distribution network. Supports omnichannel fulfillment strategies.

attributes.name: extended_cost
attributes.description: Total cost for this line item calculated as ordered quantity multiplied by unit cost. Represents the total financial commitment for this SKU on the buying order.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); FASB ASC 330 Inventory

attributes.name: gtin
attributes.description: 14-digit Global Trade Item Number for international product identification. Enables cross-border supply chain visibility and EDI transactions.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this buying order line record was last updated. Tracks changes to quantities, dates, costs, or status throughout the order lifecycle.

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of days from order placement to expected delivery. Used for replenishment planning, safety stock calculations, and vendor performance measurement.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Blue Yonder Demand Planning

attributes.name: line_number
attributes.description: Sequential line number within the buying order. Determines the ordering and display sequence of line items on the purchase order document.

attributes.name: line_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this buying order line item. Tracks progression from order placement through receipt and enables exception management for delayed or cancelled items.

attributes.name: minimum_order_quantity
attributes.description: Minimum quantity that must be ordered from the vendor for this SKU. Enforces vendor-imposed order constraints and impacts OTB planning decisions.

attributes.name: ordered_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of units ordered from the vendor for this SKU. Represents the commitment quantity for OTB (Open to Buy) tracking and receipt planning.

attributes.name: pack_size
attributes.description: Number of individual units contained in a vendor pack or case. Used for calculating total units from case quantities and for warehouse receiving operations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Standards

attributes.name: planned_margin_amount
attributes.description: Planned gross margin amount per unit calculated as retail price minus unit cost. Represents the expected profit contribution per unit sold.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: planned_margin_percent
attributes.description: Planned gross margin percentage calculated as (retail price minus unit cost) divided by retail price. Key metric for category profitability and GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); National Retail Federation (NRF) Best Practices

attributes.name: private_label_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SKU is a private label (store brand) product. Used for margin analysis, assortment strategy, and competitive positioning reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); National Retail Federation (NRF) Best Practices

attributes.name: product_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the merchandise item being ordered. Includes product name, attributes, size, color, and other distinguishing characteristics.

attributes.name: received_quantity
attributes.description: Actual quantity received to date for this line item. Used for fill rate calculation, vendor performance tracking, and identifying short shipments or overages.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: retail_price
attributes.description: Planned retail selling price for this SKU at the time of order placement. Used for initial margin calculation and pricing strategy execution.

attributes.name: sku
attributes.description: Internal stock keeping unit identifier for the merchandise item being purchased. Unique identifier used for inventory tracking and assortment management.
attributes.references: GS1 Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: store_cluster_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the store cluster or group for which this merchandise is allocated. Enables assortment planning by store type, geography, or performance tier.

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit paid to the vendor for this SKU. Represents the negotiated wholesale price and is used for COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) calculation and margin analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); FASB ASC 330 Inventory

attributes.name: upc
attributes.description: 12-digit Universal Product Code barcode identifier for the product. Used for point-of-sale scanning and supply chain tracking.

attributes.name: vendor_style_number
attributes.description: Vendor-assigned style or model number for this product. Used for cross-referencing with vendor catalogs and facilitating reorder processes.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); EDI Standards

products.name: merchandising_planogram
products.description: Master record for planograms (POGs) defining the visual merchandising layout and shelf space allocation for a category within a store or store cluster. Captures planogram name, version, effective dates, fixture type (gondola, endcap, pegboard), number of facings, shelf dimensions, and compliance status. Integrates with space planning systems.

attributes.name: merchandising_planogram_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the planogram record. Primary key.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the product category that this planogram is designed for, enabling category-specific space allocation and assortment planning.

attributes.name: cluster_id
attributes.description: Reference to the store cluster or format group that this planogram is designed for, enabling tailored assortments by store type, size, or demographic profile.

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Reference to the retail department that owns this planogram, supporting departmental merchandising strategies and accountability.

attributes.name: primary_merchandising_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandiser or category manager responsible for creating and maintaining this planogram.

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Planograms are often seasonal (seasonal_flag exists, season_name STRING exists). Currently stores season_name as string which should be normalized to season_id FK. This enables linking planogram reset

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the planogram was formally approved for deployment, marking the transition from draft to approved status.

attributes.name: compliance_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether strict compliance to this planogram is mandatory for stores, or if local merchandising teams have flexibility to adapt the layout.

attributes.name: compliance_tolerance_pct
attributes.description: Acceptable deviation percentage from the planogram specification before a store is considered non-compliant. Used in compliance audits and store execution scoring.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the planogram record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the planogram is scheduled to be retired or replaced. Nullable for open-ended planograms that remain active until explicitly superseded.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the planogram becomes active and should be implemented in stores. Critical for seasonal resets and promotional planning.

attributes.name: fixture_depth_cm
attributes.description: Depth of the fixture in centimeters, determining how far products can be placed from the front edge.

attributes.name: fixture_height_cm
attributes.description: Total height of the fixture in centimeters, defining the vertical space available across all shelves.

attributes.name: fixture_type
attributes.description: Type of physical merchandising fixture that this planogram is designed for, determining the layout constraints and display capabilities.

attributes.name: fixture_width_cm
attributes.description: Total width of the fixture in centimeters, defining the horizontal space available for product placement.

attributes.name: implementation_instructions
attributes.description: Detailed instructions for store teams on how to implement the planogram, including reset procedures, product placement guidelines, and special handling requirements.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the planogram record was last updated, supporting change tracking and version control.

attributes.name: last_reset_date
attributes.description: Date when stores last executed a full reset to this planogram, used to track implementation currency and compliance timing.

attributes.name: merchandising_planogram_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the planogram indicating whether it is in development, approved for deployment, actively in use in stores, or retired from use.

attributes.name: next_scheduled_reset_date
attributes.description: Date when the next planogram reset or refresh is scheduled, supporting forward planning and resource allocation for store operations.

attributes.name: planogram_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the planogram, typically following a POG- prefix convention used in space planning systems and merchandising communications.

attributes.name: planogram_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the planogram, typically including category and fixture type for easy identification by merchandising teams.

attributes.name: seasonal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this planogram is designed for a specific season or promotional period, requiring periodic reset and rotation.

attributes.name: shelf_count
attributes.description: Total number of shelves or levels in the fixture, determining the vertical product capacity.

attributes.name: space_allocation_sqft
attributes.description: Total square footage of selling space allocated to this planogram, calculated from fixture dimensions and used for space productivity analysis.

attributes.name: space_planning_system_code
attributes.description: External identifier from the space planning or planogram software system (e.g., JDA Space Planning, Apollo, Shelf Logic) used to create this planogram, enabling integration and synchronization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) Integration Standards

attributes.name: target_gmroi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Target Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
attributes.description: Target GMROI metric for this planogram, representing the expected gross margin dollars returned for every dollar of average inventory investment. Key performance indicator for space productivity.

attributes.name: target_sales_per_sqft
attributes.description: Target sales revenue per square foot of shelf space allocated to this planogram, used to measure space productivity and merchandising effectiveness.

attributes.name: total_facings
attributes.description: Total number of product facings (individual product positions visible to customers) allocated across all shelves in the planogram. Key metric for assortment breadth and inventory capacity.

attributes.name: total_sku_count
attributes.description: Total number of unique SKUs included in the planogram, representing the assortment depth for the category.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the planogram, allowing tracking of revisions and updates to shelf layouts over time. Typically follows semantic versioning (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0).

attributes.name: visual_merchandising_notes
attributes.description: Additional notes on visual merchandising principles, color blocking, brand adjacencies, and aesthetic considerations for this planogram.

products.name: planogram_position
products.description: Individual SKU position within a planogram defining shelf placement, facing count, minimum and maximum facings, shelf number, position sequence, and display orientation. Captures the authoritative shelf-level assortment for each planogram version. Enables compliance auditing and space productivity analysis.

attributes.name: planogram_position_id
attributes.description: Primary key for planogram_position

attributes.name: merchandising_planogram_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent planogram that contains this position. Links to the planogram master record defining the overall shelf layout.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Planogram Management

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: Planogram compliance audits, space productivity analysis, and reset execution require linking shelf positions to master SKU data for dimensions, images, and inventory integration. Essential for store

attributes.name: bay_number
attributes.description: The bay or section number within the planogram where this position is located. Defines horizontal segmentation of the fixture.

attributes.name: capacity_units
attributes.description: The total number of product units that can be stocked at this position based on the allocated space and product dimensions. Drives replenishment planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Capacity Planning

attributes.name: compliance_score
attributes.description: The compliance score (0-100%) measuring how accurately this position is executed in stores. Calculated from store audits comparing actual shelf placement to planogram specifications.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Compliance Auditing

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this planogram position record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: display_orientation
attributes.description: The orientation in which the product should be displayed at this position (e.g., front-facing, side-facing, top-facing). Impacts visual merchandising and brand presentation.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date when this planogram position is no longer active and the SKU should be removed or relocated. Nullable for open-ended positions.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Effective Dating

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date when this planogram position becomes active and the SKU should be placed at this location. Supports seasonal resets and promotional planogram changes.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Effective Dating

attributes.name: facing_count
attributes.description: The number of product facings (front-facing units visible to the customer) allocated to this SKU at this position. Drives shelf capacity and visual prominence.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Space Planning

attributes.name: fixture_type
attributes.description: The type of retail fixture where this position is located (gondola, endcap, peg hook, shelf, bin, cooler, freezer, display table). Defines the physical merchandising environment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gondola|endcap|peg_hook|shelf|bin|cooler|freezer|display_table — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NRF Store Design and Visual Merchandising Standards

attributes.name: is_hero_position
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is a hero or focal position within the planogram. Hero positions receive maximum visibility and are typically assigned to top-performing or strategic SKUs.

attributes.name: is_new_item
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this position is designated for new product introductions. Used to highlight new SKUs and drive trial purchases.

attributes.name: is_promotional
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this position is designated for promotional merchandise. Promotional positions may have temporary SKU assignments and special signage.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Promotional Planning

attributes.name: last_audit_date
attributes.description: The date when this planogram position was last audited for compliance. Used to track audit frequency and identify positions requiring re-verification.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Compliance Auditing

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this planogram position record was last modified. Tracks the most recent update to any attribute of this position.

attributes.name: maximum_facings
attributes.description: The maximum number of facings allowed for this SKU at this position. Prevents over-allocation and ensures balanced assortment presentation.

attributes.name: merchandising_zone
attributes.description: The vertical merchandising zone classification for this position (eye level, reach level, stoop level, stretch level). Eye-level positions typically drive higher sales velocity.

attributes.name: minimum_facings
attributes.description: The minimum number of facings required for this SKU to maintain adequate shelf presence and avoid out-of-stock appearance. Used for compliance auditing.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context or special instructions for this planogram position (e.g., special handling, vendor requirements, seasonal considerations).

attributes.name: position_depth_cm
attributes.description: The depth in centimeters from the front of the shelf to the back, allocated to this position. Determines how many units can be stocked front-to-back.

attributes.name: position_height_cm
attributes.description: The vertical height in centimeters allocated to this position. Defines the vertical space occupied by the product at this shelf location.

attributes.name: position_sequence
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of this position within the planogram. Used to define left-to-right or top-to-bottom placement order on the shelf.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Planogram Sequencing

attributes.name: position_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this planogram position. Active positions are currently in use; inactive positions are no longer merchandised; pending positions are scheduled for future activation.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: position_width_cm
attributes.description: The horizontal width in centimeters allocated to this position on the shelf. Used for space productivity analysis and fixture capacity planning.

attributes.name: priority_rank
attributes.description: The priority ranking of this position within the planogram. Higher-priority positions receive preferential placement and are critical for category performance.

attributes.name: sales_velocity_rank
attributes.description: The sales velocity ranking of the SKU at this position relative to other positions in the same planogram. Used to optimize high-performing SKU placement.

attributes.name: shelf_number
attributes.description: The shelf level number where this SKU is positioned. Typically numbered from bottom (1) to top, defining vertical placement within the gondola or fixture.

attributes.name: signage_required
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether special signage (price, promotional, informational) is required at this position. Drives in-store execution and compliance auditing.

attributes.name: space_productivity_index
attributes.description: A calculated index measuring the revenue or profit generated per unit of shelf space allocated to this position. Used to optimize space allocation and maximize category GMROI.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: The version number of the planogram to which this position belongs. Supports planogram versioning and historical analysis of assortment changes.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Version Control

products.name: assortment_item
products.description: Association record linking a specific SKU to an assortment plan for a given store cluster and season, serving as the single source of truth for the complete item lifecycle from onboarding through active selling to discontinuation. Captures inclusion/exclusion status, assortment role (core, seasonal, trend, clearance), planned sell-through rate, planned weeks of supply (WOS), planned AUR (Average Unit Retail), planned units. For new item onboarding: setup status, go-live date, required attributes checklist, compliance certifications (CPSC, FDA), UPC/GTIN registration status. For discontinuation: reason (low sell-through, supplier exit, assortment rationalization, dead stock), last order date, clearance strategy, and final disposition. The authoritative record of what is carried where and its complete lifecycle state.

attributes.name: assortment_item_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the assortment item record. Primary key for this association between SKU, assortment plan, store cluster, and season.

attributes.name: assortment_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent assortment plan that defines the strategic merchandise mix for a specific season and store cluster.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Assortment Planning Module

attributes.name: cluster_id
attributes.description: Reference to the store cluster grouping that this assortment item applies to. Store clusters group locations by similar demographics, performance, or format.

attributes.name: featured_campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Individual SKUs are featured in marketing campaigns as hero products, promotional items, or new arrivals. Retailers track which SKUs are featured in which campaigns for promotional planning, inventory

attributes.name: product_safety_certification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.certification. Business justification: Assortment items (especially private label, imported goods, children's products) require product safety certifications (CPSC, FDA, CE marking). Assortment planning validates certification status befor

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandising season (e.g., Spring 2024, Holiday 2024) for which this assortment item is planned.

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific product SKU included in this assortment plan.
attributes.references: GS1 Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) Standard

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary supplier providing this SKU. Critical for vendor performance tracking, negotiations, and supply chain management.

attributes.name: assortment_depth_tier
attributes.description: Classification of how many variants (sizes, colors, styles) of this item are carried within its category. Deep assortments offer extensive choice within a category, narrow assortments offer limited variety.
attributes.references: National Retail Federation (NRF) - Category Management Best Practices

attributes.name: assortment_role
attributes.description: Strategic role of this item within the assortment. Core items are year-round staples, seasonal items are time-bound, trend items capture emerging demand, clearance items are being phased out, promotional items support campaigns, and test items are being evaluated.
attributes.references: National Retail Federation (NRF) - Category Management Best Practices

attributes.name: attributes_checklist_complete
attributes.description: Indicates whether all required product attributes (dimensions, weight, materials, care instructions, etc.) have been captured in the Product Information Management (PIM) system for this SKU.
attributes.references: Informatica MDM - Product Master Data Completeness Rules

attributes.name: clearance_strategy
attributes.description: Planned approach for clearing remaining inventory of discontinued items. Markdown uses progressive price reductions, liquidation sells to third parties, RTV returns unsold units to vendor, donation gives to charity, disposal destroys unsellable goods.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Optimization

attributes.name: cpsc_certification_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) Certification Status
attributes.description: Status of CPSC safety certification for products requiring consumer safety compliance (toys, children's products, electronics, etc.). Not required for all product categories.
attributes.references: Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) - Product Safety Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assortment item record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: discontinuation_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for discontinuing this SKU from the assortment. Captures strategic rationale for removal decisions to inform future assortment planning.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this assortment item record expires and the SKU should be removed from the designated store cluster. Null for ongoing assortment items without planned end date.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Assortment Effectivity

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this assortment item record becomes active and the SKU should be available in the designated store cluster. Supports time-based assortment transitions.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Assortment Effectivity

attributes.name: fda_certification_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Certification Status
attributes.description: Status of FDA certification for food, beverage, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic products requiring regulatory approval. Not required for non-food/drug categories.
attributes.references: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) - Food Safety and Labeling Requirements

attributes.name: final_disposition_date
attributes.description: Date when all remaining inventory of this discontinued SKU must be cleared from stores and distribution centers. Marks the end of the item lifecycle in this assortment.

attributes.name: go_live_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when this SKU becomes available for sale in the designated store cluster. Critical milestone for new item launches and seasonal transitions.

attributes.name: inclusion_status
attributes.description: Current inclusion or exclusion status of this SKU in the assortment plan. Indicates whether the item is actively carried, excluded from the plan, or pending final decision.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Assortment Status Codes

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assortment item record was most recently updated. Audit trail for tracking changes to assortment decisions.

attributes.name: last_order_date
attributes.description: Final date on which purchase orders can be placed with suppliers for this SKU before discontinuation. Critical for managing inventory runout and avoiding excess stock.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Purchase Order Management

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the item lifecycle from initial onboarding through active selling to discontinuation. Tracks the complete journey of the SKU within this assortment.

attributes.name: minimum_presentation_quantity
attributes.description: Minimum number of units that must be displayed on the shelf to maintain visual impact and avoid out-of-stock perception. Used for store replenishment triggers.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the merchandising planner or system user who last modified this assortment item record. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

attributes.name: onboarding_status
attributes.description: Detailed status of new item onboarding process. Tracks progress through attribute setup, compliance certification, and go-live readiness for items in onboarding lifecycle stage.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Item Setup Workflow

attributes.name: planned_aur
attributes.description: Target average selling price per unit for this SKU during the season, accounting for planned markdowns and promotions. Used for revenue forecasting and Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) calculations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Pricing Strategy Framework

attributes.name: planned_gmroi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
attributes.description: Target Gross Margin Return on Investment for this assortment item. Measures how many dollars of gross margin are returned for every dollar invested in inventory. Key profitability metric for assortment decisions.
attributes.references: National Retail Federation (NRF) - Financial Performance Metrics

attributes.name: planned_sell_through_rate
attributes.description: Target percentage of inventory expected to sell during the season without markdown. Key metric for assortment performance planning and Open to Buy (OTB) budgeting. Expressed as percentage (e.g., 85.50 for 85.5%).
attributes.references: National Retail Federation (NRF) - Inventory Performance Metrics

attributes.name: planned_units
attributes.description: Target quantity of units to be purchased and sold for this SKU in this store cluster during the season. Foundation for Open to Buy (OTB) budget allocation.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Assortment Planning Module

attributes.name: planned_weeks_of_supply
attributes.description: Target number of weeks that planned inventory should last based on forecasted demand. Critical for replenishment planning and avoiding overstock or stockouts.
attributes.references: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Supply Coverage Metrics

attributes.name: planogram_position_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SKU requires a specific shelf position defined in store planograms. True for items with strategic placement requirements (endcaps, eye-level, checkout displays).

attributes.name: private_label_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SKU is a store brand (private label) product versus a national brand. Private label items typically have higher margins and exclusive positioning.

attributes.name: upc_registration_status
attributes.description: Status of UPC or GTIN registration with GS1 for this SKU. Required for point-of-sale scanning and supply chain tracking.
attributes.references: GS1 Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) Registration Standard

products.name: vendor_negotiation
products.description: Record of vendor negotiation events and resulting commercial terms including agreed cost prices, cost change records (old cost, new cost, effective date, reason code such as commodity inflation, contract renewal, or tariff change, buyer approval status), allowances, markdown support, co-op advertising funds, MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity), lead times, and fill rate commitments. Captures both negotiation-level header and SKU-level cost change lines as the single source of truth for all supplier commercial terms and cost adjustments. Distinct from the supplier master (owned by supplier domain). Sourced from ORMS cost management and vendor negotiation modules.

attributes.name: vendor_negotiation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the vendor negotiation event. Primary key for this data product.

attributes.name: associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or manager who provided final approval for the negotiation. Links to workforce or user master data for audit trail.

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal buyer or merchandising manager who conducted the negotiation. Links to workforce or employee master data.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary product category or department covered by this negotiation. Used for category management and assortment planning analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Category Hierarchy

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandising department responsible for this negotiation. Supports departmental GMROI and OTB budget tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Department Master

attributes.name: vendor_audit_corrective_action_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Vendor Audit Corrective Action Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.corrective_action. Business justification: Ethical sourcing programs conduct vendor audits (labor practices, safety, environmental). When violations are found, corrective action plans are negotiated into supply agreements with cost/term adjust

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the supplier or vendor involved in this negotiation. Links to the supplier master data managed by the supplier domain.

attributes.name: allowance_amount
attributes.description: Total allowance or rebate amount negotiated with the supplier, typically as a lump sum or per-unit credit. Used to calculate net cost and GMROI.

attributes.name: allowance_type
attributes.description: Classification of the allowance indicating its purpose and accounting treatment. Supports revenue recognition and vendor compliance tracking.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval status indicating whether the negotiated terms have been formally approved by the authorized buyer or merchandising manager. Required for execution.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the negotiation was formally approved. Critical for audit trail and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference to the master contract or purchase agreement that governs this negotiation. Links to contract management system for legal terms and conditions.

attributes.name: coop_advertising_fund
attributes.description: Cooperative advertising funds committed by the supplier to support joint marketing and promotional campaigns. Tracked separately for marketing budget allocation.

attributes.name: cost_change_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage change from old cost to new cost, calculated as ((new_cost - old_cost) / old_cost) * 100. Positive values indicate cost increases, negative indicate decreases.

attributes.name: cost_change_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized reason code explaining the driver of the cost change. Critical for cost variance analysis and procurement strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: commodity_inflation|contract_renewal|tariff_change|volume_discount|quality_upgrade|currency_fluctuation|freight_adjustment|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Cost Change Reason Codes

attributes.name: cost_change_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text detailed explanation of the cost change rationale provided by the buyer or supplier. Supplements the reason code with context.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this negotiation record was first created in the system. Part of standard audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this negotiation (cost prices, allowances, co-op funds). Typically base currency of the retailer.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the negotiated terms become binding and operational. Critical for cost change tracking and financial planning.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 - Revenue Recognition Effective Date

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the negotiated terms expire and require renewal or renegotiation. Nullable for open-ended agreements.

attributes.name: fill_rate_commitment_percentage
attributes.description: Supplier's committed fill rate percentage (order completion rate) as part of the service level agreement. Measured as percentage of ordered quantity delivered on time.

attributes.name: incoterms
attributes.description: International commercial terms defining the responsibilities, costs, and risks between buyer and supplier for shipment. Standard codes such as FOB, CIF, DDP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EXW|FCA|CPT|CIP|DAP|DPU|DDP|FAS|FOB|CFR|CIF — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this negotiation record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change for audit and data quality purposes.

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: Negotiated lead time in days from purchase order placement to goods receipt at distribution center. Critical for inventory planning and weeks of supply calculations.
attributes.references: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Lead Time Parameters

attributes.name: markdown_support_amount
attributes.description: Specific amount committed by the supplier to support markdown or clearance activities. Critical for margin protection and sell-through rate optimization.

attributes.name: moq
attributes.description: Minimum order quantity required by the supplier per purchase order. Critical constraint for OTB planning and replenishment strategy.

attributes.name: moq_unit_of_measure
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the MOQ field (e.g., each, case, pallet). Ensures correct interpretation of MOQ constraints.

attributes.name: negotiation_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the negotiation was concluded, either through agreement, rejection, or cancellation. Nullable for ongoing negotiations.

attributes.name: negotiation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing key discussion points, special conditions, or context from the negotiation. Supports knowledge transfer and future negotiations.

attributes.name: negotiation_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier for the vendor negotiation event, typically formatted as VN-YYYYMMDD or similar pattern used in Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Vendor Negotiation Module

attributes.name: negotiation_start_date

products.name: category_campaign_placement
products.description: This association product represents the operational placement of merchandise categories within marketing campaigns. It captures the budget allocation, sales targets, priority ranking, and featured status for each category-campaign combination. Each record links one category to one campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific promotional relationship, enabling retailers to plan, execute, and measure category-level campaign performance.. Existence Justification: In retail operations, marketing campaigns routinely feature multiple merchandise categories (e.g., a Back-to-School campaign promotes apparel, electronics, and stationery simultaneously), and each category participates in multiple campaigns throughout the year (seasonal promotions, clearance events, brand campaigns). Retailers actively manage these category-campaign placements as operational entities, setting category-specific budgets, sales targets, priority rankings, and featured status for each campaign. This is not an analytical correlation but an operational planning and execution process where marketing and merchandising teams collaborate to allocate resources and measure performance at the category-campaign intersection.

attributes.name: budget_allocation_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the total campaign budget allocated specifically to this category within this campaign. Used for planning and performance measurement.

attributes.description: Date when this category placement ends within the campaign. May differ from overall campaign end if categories are phased out or rotated.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this category placement becomes active within the campaign. May differ from overall campaign start if categories are phased in.

products.name: buyer_profit_center_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between buyer and profit_center. It captures the operational responsibility of a merchandise buyer for specific product categories within a profit center, including OTB budget allocation and time-bound accountability. Each record links one buyer to one profit_center with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling multi-dimensional buying responsibility across channels, regions, and store formats.. Existence Justification: In retail merchandising operations, buyers are assigned responsibility for specific product categories across multiple profit centers (channels, regions, store formats), and each profit center has multiple buyers managing different category portfolios. This is an operational assignment process where the business actively manages buyer-profit center responsibilities with time-bound accountability, OTB budget allocations per assignment, and category-specific scope that varies by profit center based on assortment localization and channel strategy.

products.name: category_accrual_rule
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of loyalty point accrual rules to specific merchandise categories. It captures the category-specific earning multipliers, thresholds, and effective date ranges that govern how members earn points when purchasing from specific categories. Each record links one category to one accrual rule with attributes that exist only in the context of this category-rule combination.. Existence Justification: In retail loyalty programs, merchandise categories and accrual rules have a genuine many-to-many operational relationship. A single category (e.g., Beauty) can simultaneously participate in multiple earning rules (base earning, weekend bonus, tier-specific multiplier, seasonal promotion), and a single accrual rule (e.g., '2x points on private label') applies across multiple categories (apparel, home goods, grocery). Loyalty program managers actively create, configure, and manage these category-rule assignments as part of promotional strategy and program configuration.

attributes.description: Priority ranking for conflict resolution when multiple accrual rules apply to the same category. This is relationship-specific data identified in the detection phase, supporting complex earning rule hierarchies.
