attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Facility Management; SAP S/4HANA WM Module

attributes.name: inbound_shipment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the inbound shipment record expected at this appointment. Enables traceability from appointment to physical shipment.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Inbound Shipment; SAP S/4HANA WM Module

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the purchase order associated with this inbound appointment. Links the appointment to the procurement lifecycle.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA MM Module — Purchase Order; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: scheduled_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: Receiving coordinators schedule inbound appointments for operational accountability and performance tracking. Operations managers track coordinator productivity, appointment accuracy, and dock utiliza

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the supplier or vendor originating the inbound shipment associated with this appointment.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA MM Module — Vendor Master; Informatica MDM

attributes.name: actual_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time the carrier checked in or arrived at the facility gate or dock. Used to calculate on-time performance and dwell time against the scheduled start.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Gate Check-In; NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards

attributes.name: actual_carton_count
attributes.description: The actual number of cartons or cases physically received during unloading. Discrepancies against expected carton count trigger supplier chargeback or shortage claims.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Receiving Confirmation; NRF Chargeback Standards

attributes.name: actual_pallet_count
attributes.description: The actual number of pallets received and counted during the unloading process. Compared against expected pallet count to identify discrepancies and supplier compliance issues.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Receiving Confirmation; NRF Supplier Compliance Standards

attributes.name: actual_unload_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when physical unloading was completed and the dock door was cleared. Used to compute actual unload duration and dock utilization.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Receiving Operations; NRF DC Operations Standards

attributes.name: actual_unload_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when physical unloading of the trailer or container began at the assigned dock door.

attributes.name: advance_ship_notice_number
attributes.description: The Advance Ship Notice (ASN) number transmitted by the supplier via EDI 856 prior to shipment arrival. Enables pre-receiving, labor planning, and automated appointment creation.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI 856 Advance Ship Notice (ASN); NRF EDI Standards

attributes.name: appointment_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The planned duration of the dock appointment in minutes, calculated based on expected volume (pallets/cartons) and appointment type. Drives dock door time slot blocking in the WMS scheduler.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Scheduling Engine

attributes.name: appointment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or special instructions associated with the appointment, entered by DC staff, carriers, or the scheduling system. May include special handling requirements, access instructions, or exception details.

attributes.name: appointment_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable appointment reference number used by carriers, suppliers, and DC staff to identify and communicate about the appointment. Typically generated by the WMS or carrier portal.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Scheduling; GS1 EDI Standards

attributes.name: appointment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the dock appointment. Tracks progression from initial scheduling through completion or exception. Values: scheduled (booked but not confirmed), confirmed (carrier acknowledged), arrived (carrier checked in at gate), completed (unload finished), no_show (carrier did not arrive), cancelled (appointment voided).
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Lifecycle; NRF Supply Chain Standards

attributes.name: appointment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the inbound appointment by unloading method. Live unload: carrier waits while freight is unloaded. Drop trailer: carrier leaves trailer at dock for later unloading. Cross-dock (cross-docking): freight transferred directly to outbound without storage. Floor load: loose cartons loaded directly on trailer floor.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Type Configuration; NRF DC Operations Standards

attributes.name: bill_of_lading_number
attributes.description: The Bill of Lading (BOL) number issued by the carrier as a receipt of freight and contract of carriage. Key document for inbound receiving reconciliation and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI 856 Advance Ship Notice (ASN); Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)

attributes.name: carrier_scac_code
attributes.description: The Standard Carrier Alpha Code (SCAC) assigned by the National Motor Freight Traffic Association (NMFTA) to uniquely identify the transportation carrier. Used in EDI transactions and freight audit.
attributes.references: NMFTA SCAC Code Registry; GS1 EDI 214 Transportation Carrier Shipment Status

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the appointment record was first created in the system, regardless of scheduling source. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; FASB ASC 606 Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: dock_door_number
attributes.description: The specific dock door or bay number at the facility assigned to this inbound appointment. Used for physical routing of labor and equipment to the correct location.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Dock Door Management

attributes.name: dock_door_zone
attributes.description: The physical zone or section of the facility where the assigned dock door is located (e.g., North Dock, Receiving Zone A). Supports labor planning and traffic flow management.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Facility Zone Configuration

attributes.name: driver_license_number
attributes.description: The commercial driver's license (CDL) number of the driver presenting at the facility. Captured for security verification and regulatory compliance at gate check-in.
attributes.references: FMCSA Commercial Driver License (CDL) Requirements 49 CFR Part 383; OSHA Facility Security

attributes.name: driver_name
attributes.description: The name of the truck driver who checked in at the facility for this appointment. Captured at gate check-in for security and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 — Workplace Safety; FMCSA Driver Identification Requirements

attributes.name: expected_carton_count
attributes.description: The total number of cartons or cases expected in the inbound shipment per the ASN or purchase order. Used for receiving accuracy validation.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI 856 ASN; Manhattan Associates WMS — Receiving

attributes.name: expected_pallet_count
attributes.description: The number of pallets expected to be unloaded during this appointment as communicated via ASN or purchase order. Used for dock labor planning and time slot duration calculation.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Capacity Planning; GS1 SSCC

attributes.name: expected_weight_kg
attributes.description: The total expected gross weight of the inbound shipment in kilograms as declared on the Bill of Lading or ASN. Used for dock equipment planning and freight audit.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI 856 ASN; FMCSA Weight Regulations

attributes.name: is_hazmat
attributes.description: Indicates whether the inbound shipment contains hazardous materials (Hazmat) requiring special handling, dock equipment, or regulatory compliance procedures at the facility.
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) — Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) 49 CFR; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200

attributes.name: is_temperature_controlled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the inbound shipment requires temperature-controlled handling (refrigerated or frozen). Triggers assignment to a temperature-controlled dock door and cold chain receiving procedures.
attributes.references: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) — Sanitary Transportation Rule; CPSC Cold Chain Standards

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the appointment record was most recently modified. Tracks status changes, reschedules, and data corrections for audit and change management purposes.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; Manhattan Associates WMS — Change Audit

attributes.name: late_arrival_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason captured when a carrier arrives outside the scheduled appointment window. Used for root cause analysis of inbound logistics delays and carrier performance management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: traffic|weather|mechanical_breakdown|driver_hours|customs_delay|shipper_delay|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NRF Carrier Compliance Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS — Exception Management

attributes.name: on_time_arrival_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier arrived within the scheduled appointment window. Derived from comparison of actual arrival timestamp to scheduled start timestamp. Used for carrier on-time performance (OTP) reporting and SLA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: NRF Carrier Performance Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS — Carrier Scorecard

attributes.name: original_scheduled_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The original planned appointment start timestamp before any rescheduling occurred. Preserved for compliance reporting and to measure the impact of rescheduling on DC operations.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Audit Trail

attributes.name: pro_number
attributes.description: The carrier-assigned Progressive (PRO) number, which is the freight bill number used to track the shipment through the carrier's system. Standard identifier for LTL and TL freight.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI 214 Transportation Carrier Shipment Status; NRF Freight Standards

attributes.name: reschedule_count
attributes.description: The number of times this appointment has been rescheduled. High reschedule counts indicate carrier reliability issues or supply chain disruptions and are used in supplier/carrier compliance scoring.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment History; NRF Supplier Compliance Standards

attributes.name: scheduled_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when the unloading activity is expected to be completed and the dock door released for the next appointment.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Scheduling; ISO 8601

attributes.name: scheduled_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when the carrier is expected to arrive at the dock door and unloading is scheduled to begin. Principal business event timestamp for the appointment.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Appointment Scheduling; ISO 8601

attributes.name: scheduling_source
attributes.description: Channel or method through which the appointment was originally created. Carrier portal: self-service web portal. EDI: Electronic Data Interchange automated scheduling. Manual: DC staff entered directly. API: programmatic integration from TMS or OMS.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI Standards (EDI 214); Manhattan Associates WMS — Scheduling Source

attributes.name: seal_number
attributes.description: The security seal number affixed to the trailer or container door. Verified at arrival to confirm shipment integrity and detect tampering during transit.
attributes.references: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) — Cargo Security; ISO 17712 High-Security Seals

attributes.name: temperature_requirement
attributes.description: The specific temperature handling requirement for the inbound shipment. Ambient: room temperature. Chilled: 0–4°C. Frozen: -18°C or below. Ultra-frozen: -40°C or below (e.g., pharmaceutical or specialty frozen goods).
attributes.references: FDA FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule; ISO 22000 Food Safety Management

attributes.name: trailer_number
attributes.description: The carrier-assigned trailer or container identification number for the inbound shipment. Used for physical asset tracking, seal verification, and RFID scanning at the dock.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS — Trailer Management; GS1 SSCC Standards

products.name: cross_dock_plan
products.description: Cross-docking execution plans for merchandise flowing directly from inbound receiving to outbound shipping without DC storage. Captures source PO, destination store allocations, SKU-level quantities, planned and actual cross-dock dates, cross-dock type (pre-allocated, opportunistic flow-through), execution status, and handling instructions. Reduces DC handling costs and accelerates store replenishment for high-velocity and promotional merchandise.

attributes.name: cross_dock_plan_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the cross-dock execution plan record. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; GS1 Supply Chain Standards

attributes.name: dc_facility_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Distribution Center (DC) facility where the cross-dock operation is executed. Links to the DC master record.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; SAP S/4HANA Retail WM Module

attributes.name: inbound_asn_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the inbound Advance Shipment Notice (ASN) from the supplier, confirming the shipment details and expected arrival of merchandise to be cross-docked.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the destination retail store to which the cross-docked merchandise is allocated and shipped. For multi-store plans, this represents the primary or single destination store.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); SAP S/4HANA Retail SD Module

attributes.name: merchandise_category_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the merchandise category (e.g., grocery, apparel, electronics) to which the cross-docked SKU belongs. Used for category-level cross-dock performance reporting and assortment planning alignment.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC)

attributes.name: outbound_carrier_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transportation carrier or Third-Party Logistics (3PL) provider responsible for delivering cross-docked merchandise from the DC to the destination store.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Retail SD Module; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: planner_associate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: Cross-dock planners create plans for planning accountability and performance tracking. Supply chain tracks plan accuracy, dwell time, and execution success by planner for operational efficiency and KP

attributes.name: promo_campaign_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the promotional event driving this cross-dock plan, if applicable. High-velocity promotional merchandise is a primary use case for cross-docking to accelerate store replenishment.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

attributes.name: replenishment_plan_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the replenishment plan that triggered this cross-dock execution. Links to the demand-driven replenishment plan generated by the forecasting and replenishment system.
attributes.references: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) being cross-docked. Links to the product master record for item-level tracking and allocation.
attributes.references: GS1 Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: supply_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the inbound Purchase Order (PO) from which merchandise is being cross-docked. Links to the purchase order header record in the procurement system.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the supplier or vendor delivering the inbound merchandise for cross-docking. Used for supplier performance tracking and EDI coordination.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module; Informatica MDM

attributes.name: actual_carton_qty
attributes.description: The actual number of cartons processed through the cross-dock operation. Used to reconcile against planned carton count and measure DC handling accuracy.

attributes.name: actual_inbound_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which inbound merchandise arrived at the Distribution Center (DC). Compared against planned inbound date to measure supplier on-time delivery performance.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards

attributes.name: actual_inbound_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when inbound merchandise was received at the DC dock door. Used for dwell time calculation and cross-dock cycle time analytics.

attributes.name: actual_outbound_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which cross-docked merchandise departed the Distribution Center (DC) for the destination store. Used to measure DC throughput speed and cross-dock execution efficiency.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards

attributes.name: actual_outbound_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when cross-docked merchandise departed the DC on the outbound carrier. Used to calculate total DC dwell time and cross-dock cycle time.

attributes.name: actual_received_unit_qty
attributes.description: The actual number of units received from the supplier at the DC inbound dock. Compared against planned quantity to identify short shipments, overages, or discrepancies.

attributes.name: actual_shipped_unit_qty
attributes.description: The actual number of units shipped outbound to the destination store after cross-docking. May differ from received quantity due to damage, quality holds, or allocation adjustments.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Supply Chain Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this cross-dock plan record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and operational reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

attributes.name: cross_dock_type
attributes.description: Classification of the cross-docking method. Pre-allocated means merchandise is pre-sorted for specific stores before arrival; opportunistic (flow-through) means merchandise is sorted upon arrival based on real-time demand signals. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pre_allocated|opportunistic|flow_through|merge_in_transit|pool_distribution — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NRF Supply Chain Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: dwell_time_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours merchandise spent at the Distribution Center (DC) between inbound receipt and outbound shipment. A key cross-dock efficiency metric; target is typically under 24 hours for true cross-docking.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards

attributes.name: fill_rate_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the planned unit quantity that was actually fulfilled and shipped to the destination store through this cross-dock plan. Calculated as (actual_shipped_unit_qty / planned_unit_qty) * 100. Key supply chain KPI for cross-dock execution performance.
attributes.references: NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

attributes.name: handling_instructions
attributes.description: Free-text operational instructions for DC associates handling the cross-dock merchandise, such as fragile handling, temperature requirements, sequencing rules, or special labeling requirements.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; OSHA Workplace Safety Standards

attributes.name: inbound_dock_door
attributes.description: The assigned inbound dock door number or identifier at the Distribution Center where the supplier's truck will unload merchandise for cross-docking.

attributes.name: is_hazmat
attributes.description: Indicates whether the cross-docked merchandise contains hazardous materials requiring special handling, labeling, and transport compliance per regulatory standards.
attributes.references: OSHA Hazard Communication Standard; CPSC Product Safety Standards

attributes.name: is_private_label
attributes.description: Indicates whether the cross-docked merchandise is a Private Label (store brand) product. Private label merchandise may have distinct handling, labeling, and compliance requirements.
attributes.references: FTC Labeling Standards; NRF Private Label Standards

attributes.name: is_promotional_merchandise
attributes.description: Indicates whether the merchandise in this cross-dock plan is associated with a promotional event. Promotional merchandise is a primary driver of cross-docking to accelerate store replenishment and reduce DC handling costs.
attributes.references: NRF Retail Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this cross-dock plan record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

attributes.name: outbound_dock_door
attributes.description: The assigned outbound dock door number or identifier at the Distribution Center from which cross-docked merchandise will be loaded onto the outbound carrier for store delivery.

attributes.name: outbound_trailer_number
attributes.description: The trailer or container number assigned for the outbound shipment of cross-docked merchandise to the destination store. Used for load tracking and carrier coordination.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; GS1 Transport Standards

attributes.name: plan_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments added by DC planners or operations managers regarding exceptions, adjustments, or special circumstances related to this cross-dock plan.

attributes.name: plan_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the cross-dock plan, used in operational communications between DC teams, suppliers, and store operations. Follows the format CDP-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; GS1 Supply Chain Standards

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the cross-dock execution plan. Tracks progression from initial planning through execution to completion or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|planned|in_progress|completed|cancelled|on_hold — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Supply Chain Standards

attributes.name: planned_carton_qty
attributes.description: The planned number of cartons (cases) of the SKU scheduled for cross-docking. Used for dock door capacity planning, pallet build, and outbound trailer loading.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; GS1 Logistics Standards

attributes.name: planned_inbound_date
attributes.description: The planned date on which inbound merchandise from the supplier is expected to arrive at the Distribution Center (DC) for cross-docking. Used for dock scheduling and labor planning.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

attributes.name: planned_inbound_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise planned date and time for inbound merchandise arrival at the DC dock door. Used for granular dock door scheduling and labor allocation within the WMS.

attributes.name: planned_outbound_date
attributes.description: The planned date on which cross-docked merchandise is scheduled to depart the Distribution Center (DC) for the destination store. Drives outbound dock scheduling and carrier booking.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

attributes.name: planned_pallet_qty
attributes.description: The planned number of pallets expected for this cross-dock plan. Used for outbound trailer capacity planning and dock door assignment.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; GS1 Logistics Standards

attributes.name: planned_unit_qty
attributes.description: The planned number of individual units (eaches) of the SKU scheduled for cross-docking under this plan. Drives inbound receiving expectations and outbound load planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: temperature_requirement
attributes.description: Temperature handling requirement for the cross-docked merchandise. Critical for grocery and perishable categories to ensure cold chain compliance during DC cross-dock operations.
attributes.references: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA); CPSC Product Safety Standards

attributes.name: variance_unit_qty
attributes.description: The difference between planned unit quantity and actual shipped unit quantity for this cross-dock plan. Positive values indicate a shortfall; negative values indicate an overage. Used for supplier compliance and chargeback management.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Vendor Compliance Standards

products.name: supplychain_edi_transaction
products.description: EDI transaction log for supply chain document exchanges with suppliers, 3PLs, and trading partners via SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, or similar VAN. Captures transaction set type (850 PO, 855 PO Ack, 856 ASN, 810 Invoice, 860 PO Change, 997 Functional Ack), trading partner GLN/DUNS, transmission timestamp, direction (inbound/outbound), document reference, processing status, error codes, retry count, and compliance score. Enables EDI compliance monitoring against retailer routing guide requirements, SLA breach detection for late ASN/invoice, integration health dashboards, and trading partner onboarding validation.

attributes.name: supplychain_edi_transaction_id
attributes.description: Primary key for edi_transaction

attributes.name: dc_facility_id
attributes.description: The EDI interchange receiver identifier (ISA08) as defined in the interchange control header. Identifies the intended recipient of the EDI transmission. May be the trading partner's EDI ID (outbound) or the retailer's EDI ID (inbound).
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA08 Segment Specification

attributes.name: item_cross_reference_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.item_cross_reference. Business justification: EDI document processing (850 PO, 856 ASN) requires mapping trading partner item numbers to internal SKUs. Cross-reference table provides this translation during inbound EDI transaction parsing, enabli

attributes.name: sender_vendor_id
attributes.description: The EDI interchange sender identifier (ISA06) as defined in the interchange control header. Identifies the originating party of the EDI transmission. May be the retailer's EDI ID (outbound) or the trading partner's EDI ID (inbound).
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA06 Segment Specification

attributes.name: shipment_id
attributes.description: The shipment or ASN reference number extracted from the EDI document payload (e.g., BSN02 on 856 ASN). Links the EDI transaction to the physical shipment record in Manhattan Associates WMS for inbound receiving and cross-docking workflows.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 856 ASN BSN Segment; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Surrogate identifier referencing the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or logistics provider) involved in this EDI transaction. Links to the supplier/trading partner master record for onboarding validation and compliance scoring.
attributes.references: GS1 GLN Standard; ANSI ASC X12; Informatica MDM

attributes.name: compliance_score
attributes.description: A numeric score (0.00–100.00) representing the degree of compliance of this EDI transaction against the retailer's routing guide requirements and EDI standards. Calculated by the VAN or integration platform based on segment completeness, data element accuracy, and timing adherence. Drives trading partner scorecards and chargeback assessments.
attributes.references: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI Compliance Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this EDI transaction record was first created in the Silver layer data product. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security Management; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the EDI document was received from a trading partner (INBOUND) or sent to a trading partner (OUTBOUND) by the retailer. Critical for routing guide compliance monitoring and SLA tracking.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: document_reference_number
attributes.description: The business document reference number embedded within the EDI transaction, such as the Purchase Order number (850), Invoice number (810), or ASN shipment reference (856). Enables cross-referencing with source documents in SAP S/4HANA MM, Oracle RMS, or Manhattan WMS.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 BEG/BIG/BSN Segment; GS1 EDI; SAP S/4HANA MM

attributes.name: document_size_bytes
attributes.description: The size of the raw EDI document payload in bytes. Used for VAN transmission cost allocation, integration platform capacity planning, and anomaly detection (e.g., unusually large or empty documents).
attributes.references: GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: edi_standard
attributes.description: The EDI messaging standard used for this transaction (e.g., ANSI X12 for North American retail, EDIFACT for international trading partners, TRADACOMS for UK retail). Determines parsing rules and compliance validation logic.
attributes.references: GS1 EDI; ANSI ASC X12; UN/EDIFACT ISO 9735

attributes.name: edi_version
attributes.description: The version of the EDI standard used for this transaction (e.g., '004010', '005010', '006020' for ANSI X12; 'D96A', 'D01B' for EDIFACT). Version determines segment and element specifications for validation.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA12 Version Identifier; GS1 EDI

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: The primary error code returned when an EDI transaction fails validation or processing (e.g., ANSI X12 AK304 error codes: 1=Unrecognized segment, 2=Unexpected segment, 3=Mandatory segment missing, 8=Segment has data element errors). Supports error triage and trading partner remediation.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 AK3/AK4 Error Codes; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: error_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the error or validation failure for this EDI transaction. Provides context for error resolution, trading partner notification, and chargeback dispute management.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 AK3/AK4 Error Codes; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: functional_ack_status
attributes.description: The acknowledgment status returned in the 997 Functional Acknowledgment or 999 Implementation Acknowledgment for this transaction. Indicates whether the trading partner accepted, accepted with errors, or rejected the EDI document. Critical for EDI compliance monitoring and chargeback prevention.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 997/999 Transaction Set; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: functional_ack_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the 997 Functional Acknowledgment was received for this transaction. Used to calculate acknowledgment turnaround time and detect SLA breaches for late acknowledgments per retailer routing guide requirements.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 997 Transaction Set; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: group_control_number
attributes.description: The control number assigned to the functional group (GS06 segment) within the EDI interchange. Groups related transaction sets of the same type and enables functional acknowledgment (997) matching at the group level.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 GS06 Segment Specification

attributes.name: interchange_control_number
attributes.description: The unique 9-digit control number assigned to the EDI interchange envelope (ISA13 segment). Used to uniquely identify and track each interchange transmission for deduplication, acknowledgment matching, and audit purposes.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA13 Segment Specification

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The supplier invoice number extracted from the EDI 810 Invoice transaction payload (BIG02 segment). Used to match EDI invoices against purchase orders and receipts in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO for three-way match and accounts payable processing.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 810 Invoice BIG Segment; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: processed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the EDI transaction was fully processed and accepted or rejected by the downstream system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA MM, Oracle RMS). Used to measure end-to-end processing latency and SLA adherence.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 997 Functional Acknowledgment; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: processing_status
attributes.description: Current processing lifecycle state of the EDI transaction within the VAN/integration platform. Drives SLA breach detection, retry workflows, and integration health dashboards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RECEIVED|QUEUED|PROCESSING|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|ERROR|RETRYING|ACKNOWLEDGED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 997 Functional Acknowledgment; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: The retailer's Purchase Order number associated with this EDI transaction, extracted from the document payload (e.g., BEG02 on 850, BIG04 on 810, BSN02 on 856). Enables cross-referencing with SAP S/4HANA MM purchase orders and Oracle RMS procurement records.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 BEG/BIG/BSN Segment; SAP S/4HANA MM; Oracle RMS

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the EDI document was received and ingested by the retailer's integration platform or VAN. Used to calculate transmission latency and inbound SLA compliance windows.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Control Header; NRF EDI Routing Guide

attributes.name: retry_count
attributes.description: The number of times this EDI transaction has been retried after an initial failure or rejection. Used to identify persistently failing transactions, trigger escalation workflows, and monitor integration platform health.

attributes.name: routing_guide_version
attributes.description: The version of the retailer's EDI routing guide against which this transaction was validated (e.g., 'v2024.1'). Enables compliance scoring to be evaluated against the correct version of requirements, supporting trading partner onboarding and annual routing guide updates.
attributes.references: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI Compliance Framework

attributes.name: segment_count
attributes.description: The total number of segments in the EDI transaction set as reported in the SE02 trailer segment. Used for document integrity validation — the received segment count must match the SE02 value to confirm complete transmission.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 SE02 Transaction Set Trailer; GS1 EDI

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this EDI transaction breached the retailer's routing guide SLA requirement (True = SLA breached, False = within SLA). Populated based on comparison of transmission_timestamp against sla_target_hours. Drives SLA breach alerts and chargeback workflows.
attributes.references: NRF EDI Routing Guide; FTC Advertising Standards

attributes.name: sla_target_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: EDI Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Hours
attributes.description: The contractual SLA target in hours within which this EDI transaction type must be transmitted and acknowledged per the retailer's routing guide (e.g., ASN must be sent within 24 hours of shipment). Used as the benchmark for SLA breach detection.
attributes.references: NRF EDI Routing Guide; SLA Definition

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record that originated or will consume this EDI transaction (e.g., SAP_S4HANA for PO/Invoice, MANHATTAN_WMS for ASN/receiving, ORACLE_RMS for merchandise orders). Supports integration health monitoring and system-level error attribution.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA MM; Oracle RMS; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: test_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the EDI interchange is a test transmission (T) or a production transmission (P) as specified in the ISA15 segment. Test transactions must be excluded from operational processing and compliance scoring.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA15 Segment Specification

attributes.name: trading_partner_duns
attributes.business_glossary_term: Trading Partner Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number
attributes.description: The Dun & Bradstreet DUNS number of the trading partner, a 9-digit identifier used for supplier identity verification, credit risk assessment, and EDI partner onboarding validation.
attributes.references: Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Standard; ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Header

attributes.name: trading_partner_gln
attributes.description: The GS1 Global Location Number (GLN) of the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or DC) involved in this EDI exchange. A 13-digit GS1 identifier used to uniquely identify legal entities and physical locations in the supply chain. Required for GS1-compliant EDI routing.
attributes.references: GS1 GLN Standard; GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Guidelines

attributes.name: trading_partner_name
attributes.description: The registered business name of the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or logistics provider) as maintained in the EDI partner profile. Supports human-readable reporting and onboarding dashboards.
attributes.references: Informatica MDM; GS1 EDI Partner Profile

attributes.name: trading_partner_qualifier
attributes.description: The ANSI X12 ISA qualifier code indicating the type of trading partner identifier used in the interchange (e.g., 01=DUNS, 08=UCC EDI Comm ID, 12=Phone, 14=DUNS+4, 20=Health Industry Number, ZZ=Mutually Defined). Required for EDI interchange routing.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Segment Specification; GS1 EDI

attributes.name: transaction_control_number
attributes.description: The control number assigned to the individual transaction set (ST02 segment) within the functional group. Uniquely identifies a single transaction set for acknowledgment and error tracking.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ST02 Segment Specification

attributes.name: transaction_set_code
attributes.description: The ANSI X12 or EDIFACT transaction set number identifying the document type exchanged (e.g., 850 Purchase Order, 855 PO Acknowledgment, 856 Advance Ship Notice, 810 Invoice, 860 PO Change Order, 997 Functional Acknowledgment, 832 Price/Sales Catalog, 846 Inventory Inquiry). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 850|855|856|810|860|997|832|846|753|754 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Guidelines

attributes.name: transaction_set_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the EDI transaction set type (e.g., 'Purchase Order', 'Advance Ship Notice (ASN)', 'Invoice', 'Functional Acknowledgment') corresponding to the transaction_set_id. Supports dashboards and reporting without requiring code lookups.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; GS1 EDI

attributes.name: transmission_protocol
attributes.description: The communication protocol used to transmit the EDI document (e.g., AS2, SFTP, FTP, HTTPS, VAN mailbox, AS4). Relevant for integration health dashboards and security compliance audits per ISO 27001.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12; AS2 RFC 4130; ISO 27001

attributes.name: transmission_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the EDI document was transmitted over the VAN or direct connection. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for SLA measurement and audit trails.
attributes.references: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Control Header; GS1 EDI

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this EDI transaction record was last modified in the Silver layer data product, such as when processing status changed or retry count incremented.

attributes.name: van_provider
attributes.description: The Value-Added Network (VAN) or direct EDI integration provider used to transmit this transaction (e.g., SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, Sterling Commerce, OpenText, Direct AS2/SFTP). Supports integration health monitoring and VAN cost allocation.
attributes.references: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI

products.name: dc_facility
products.description: Master record for each distribution center (DC) and micro-fulfillment center (MFC) operated by Retail. Captures facility type (regional DC, MFC, dark store, cross-dock hub, returns center), physical address, square footage, storage capacity (pallet positions, cubic feet), temperature zones (ambient, chilled, frozen), dock door count, operating hours, facility status (active, planned, decommissioned), owning region, and Manhattan WMS instance assignment. SSOT for DC/MFC identity referenced by all distribution operations including zone layout, dock scheduling, carrier assignments, and performance tracking.
products.reference: Distribution Center Master / WMS Facility Master

attributes.name: dc_facility_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the distribution center or micro-fulfillment center facility. Primary key for the DC facility master record.

attributes.name: address_line_1
attributes.description: Primary street address line for the facility (street number, street name, building identifier).

attributes.name: address_line_2
attributes.description: Secondary address line for additional location details (suite, floor, building name) if applicable.

attributes.name: automation_level
attributes.description: Classification of the facility's warehouse automation maturity: manual (labor-intensive), semi-automated (some mechanization), highly automated (extensive robotics and conveyors), or fully automated (lights-out operations).

attributes.name: bonded_warehouse_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility is a customs-bonded warehouse authorized to store imported goods before duties and taxes are paid, enabling deferred duty payment and re-export options.
attributes.references: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Bonded Warehouse Regulations

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality where the facility is located.

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: Date when the facility was permanently closed or decommissioned. Null for active facilities.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the facility is located (e.g., 'USA', 'CAN', 'MEX').

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this facility record was first created in the master data system.

attributes.name: dock_door_count
attributes.description: Total number of loading dock doors available for inbound receiving and outbound shipping operations.

attributes.name: facility_code
attributes.description: Business-assigned unique alphanumeric code for the facility used in operational systems, shipping documents, and cross-system integration. Typically 4-12 characters.

attributes.name: facility_email_address
attributes.description: Primary email address for the facility used for operational communications, appointment confirmations, and document exchange.

attributes.name: facility_manager_name
attributes.description: Full name of the facility manager or site director responsible for day-to-day operations and performance.

attributes.name: facility_name
attributes.description: Official business name of the distribution center or fulfillment facility (e.g., 'Northeast Regional DC', 'Manhattan MFC-01').

attributes.name: facility_phone_number
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for the facility used for carrier coordination, supplier communication, and operational inquiries.

attributes.name: facility_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the facility. Active facilities are fully operational; planned facilities are approved but not yet built; under construction facilities are being built; decommissioned facilities are permanently closed; temporarily closed facilities are inactive but may reopen; seasonal facilities operate only during peak periods.

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Classification of the facility based on its primary operational purpose: regional DC (large-scale distribution), micro-fulfillment center (MFC for rapid e-commerce), dark store (fulfillment-only, no retail), cross-dock hub (transshipment), returns center (reverse logistics), or forward stocking location (FSL).

attributes.name: gln
attributes.description: GS1-issued 13-digit Global Location Number uniquely identifying this facility in global supply chain transactions and EDI exchanges.

attributes.name: hazmat_certified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility is certified and equipped to handle, store, and ship hazardous materials in compliance with DOT and OSHA regulations.

attributes.name: inbound_dock_door_count
attributes.description: Number of dock doors dedicated to inbound receiving operations from suppliers and carriers.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this facility record was most recently modified in the master data system.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the facility in decimal degrees for mapping, routing, and geospatial analytics.

attributes.name: lease_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the current facility lease agreement expires. Null for owned facilities. Used for lease renewal planning and financial forecasting.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the facility in decimal degrees for mapping, routing, and geospatial analytics.

attributes.name: opened_date
attributes.description: Date when the facility first became operational and began processing inventory and orders.

attributes.name: operating_hours_weekday
attributes.description: Standard operating hours for the facility on weekdays (Monday-Friday) in format 'HH:MM-HH:MM' (e.g., '06:00-22:00'). Used for appointment scheduling and labor planning.

attributes.name: operating_hours_weekend
attributes.description: Standard operating hours for the facility on weekends (Saturday-Sunday) in format 'HH:MM-HH:MM'. May differ from weekday hours or indicate closed status.

attributes.name: outbound_dock_door_count
attributes.description: Number of dock doors dedicated to outbound shipping operations to stores, customers, or other facilities.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility is owned by the company, leased from a landlord, or operated by a third-party logistics provider (3PL). Impacts financial reporting and operational control.

attributes.name: owning_region_code
attributes.description: Business region or geographic division code that owns and manages this facility (e.g., 'NORTHEAST', 'WEST', 'CENTRAL'). Used for organizational hierarchy and P&L reporting.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the facility address used for mail delivery and geographic routing.

attributes.name: state_province_code
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-2 subdivision code for the state, province, or region (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'ON' for Ontario).

attributes.name: storage_capacity_cubic_feet
attributes.description: Total volumetric storage capacity of the facility measured in cubic feet, accounting for vertical storage utilization.

attributes.name: storage_capacity_pallet_positions
attributes.description: Maximum number of standard pallet positions available for inventory storage in racking and floor storage.

attributes.name: temperature_zone_ambient_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility has ambient temperature storage zones (room temperature, non-climate-controlled) for general merchandise.

attributes.name: temperature_zone_chilled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility has refrigerated (chilled) storage zones typically maintained at 32-40°F for perishable goods like dairy and produce.

attributes.name: temperature_zone_frozen_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility has frozen storage zones typically maintained at 0°F or below for frozen foods and ice cream.

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the facility location (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'America/Chicago') used for scheduling and timestamp normalization.

attributes.name: total_square_footage
attributes.description: Total building square footage of the facility including warehouse space, office space, and support areas. Measured in square feet.

attributes.name: twenty_four_seven_operation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the facility operates continuously 24 hours per day, 7 days per week to support high-volume or time-sensitive fulfillment requirements.

attributes.name: warehouse_square_footage
attributes.description: Square footage dedicated to warehouse operations including storage, picking, packing, and staging areas. Measured in square feet.

attributes.name: wms_instance_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the Manhattan WMS instance or system deployment that manages this facility's warehouse operations. Used for system integration and data routing.

products.name: warehouse_zone
products.description: Defines the complete physical layout hierarchy within a DC or MFC, from zones (receiving, bulk storage, forward pick, packing, staging, dispatch, returns) down to individual storage locations (bin, slot, shelf, pallet position, floor stack). Zone-level attributes include zone code, type, temperature classification (ambient, chilled, frozen), aisle range, rack configuration (selective, drive-in, push-back, flow), automation type (manual, conveyor, AS/RS, shuttle, AMR), and zone capacity metrics. Location-level attributes include location code, aisle, bay, level, position, location type (bulk, pick face, reserve, floor, overflow), weight capacity, cubic capacity, RFID/barcode tag, and current occupancy status. SSOT for all physical space definitions within a facility — supports slotting optimization, pick path planning, capacity management, and location-level inventory tracking within Manhattan WMS.

products.name: inbound_shipment
products.description: Tracks inbound shipments arriving at a DC or MFC from suppliers, vendors, or inter-facility transfers. Captures ASN (Advance Ship Notice) reference, carrier, trailer number, expected and actual arrival date/time, PO references, total carton and pallet counts, shipment status (in-transit, arrived, receiving, closed), and temperature compliance flag for cold chain shipments. Integrates with EDI 856 ASN feeds and Manhattan WMS receiving workflows. SSOT for all inbound freight visibility at the distribution center level.

Records dock door assignment, unload start/end timestamps, cartons received vs. expected, discrepancy flags (overage, shortage, damage), receiver employee ID, pallet count, and blind vs. directed receiving mode. Each receiving event is tied to an inbound shipment and drives put-away task generation in Manhattan WMS.

products.name: warehouse_task
products.description: Represents any directed warehouse task generated within Manhattan WMS, covering putaway, picking, replenishment, cycle count, and internal movement task types. Captures task type discriminator (putaway, discrete_pick, cluster_pick, batch_pick, zone_pick, replenishment, move), SKU, quantity, lot/expiry, source location, target location, assigned operator, equipment type (forklift, reach truck, conveyor, AMR), task priority, task status (pending, assigned, in-progress, completed, short, cancelled), creation timestamp, completion timestamp, substitution flag, and exception reason. Unified SSOT for all directed work within the DC — eliminates separate putaway and pick task entities in favor of a single task management model consistent with Manhattan WMS task interleaving and labor optimization.

products.name: outbound_order
products.description: Represents a distribution outbound order directing the DC or MFC to fulfill and ship goods to a destination (store, customer, 3PL node). Captures order type (store replenishment, e-commerce, BOPIS, DSD bypass, inter-DC transfer), destination node, requested ship date, required delivery date, priority level, total lines/units/weight/cube, wave assignment, and order status lifecycle (released, waved, picking, packed, shipped, closed). For store replenishment: captures replenishment type (push, pull, min-max, VMI), replenishment reason, demand planning source reference, and replenishment frequency. Central transactional entity for all DC outbound execution including store replenishment, e-commerce fulfillment, and inter-facility transfers.
